goal: Implement the first real coding-agent bridge for CodeMemory: a manual-first start/query/capture/finish flow that a Codex task can invoke without depending on hidden desktop hooks, and validate it end-to-end against a Project_J task.
success_criteria: A thin local bridge exposes deterministic start, memory query, event capture/batch, and finish operations over the existing event and card APIs.
The bridge preserves project/task/session identity, event ordering, idempotency, completeness, and existing redaction boundaries without writing SQLite directly.
A Codex-specific project skill/instruction documents the manual lifecycle and produces an allowlisted coding evidence package.
A real Project_J smoke task can query prior memory, append a bounded event stream, trigger extraction/consolidation, and retrieve the resulting card or report.
Focused bridge tests, full regression, lint, compile, and a localhost API smoke pass; no hidden Codex API or automatic hook is required.
constraints: SQLite remains the canonical store and the bridge uses the existing IngestService or public HTTP surface.
Manual-first is the required compatibility path; automatic hooks, MCP server packaging, and transcript interception are out of scope.
Only visible, allowlisted coding evidence may be captured; hidden reasoning, credentials, host instructions, and unrelated plugin text are excluded.
Project_J verification remains read-only and bounded by the existing manifest contract.
JSONL is a replay/failure fallback only; localhost HTTP or the shared service is the primary transport.
non_goals: Native Codex Desktop hook or private app database integration
Production MCP server, authentication, or remote hosting
stop_condition: Stop after the manual bridge, Codex skill instructions, Project_J smoke evidence, focused/full verification, and documentation are complete; leave automatic hooks as a separately evaluated next phase.
